summary: The Codex Gigas, or Devil's Bible, is the largest known medieval manuscript: 310 leaves, 92 cm tall and about 75 kg. It holds the Latin Bible, the works of Josephus, Isidore's Etymologiae, medical texts and a chronicle of Bohemia. Its famous full-page Devil faces a picture of the Kingdom of Heaven. Legend says one monk wrote it in a single night with help from the Devil.
context: The book was made between 1204 and 1230 at the Podlazice monastery at Chrast in Bohemia. Swedish troops took it in 1648 when they seized Prague, and it has been in Stockholm since 1649. It was thrown from a window during the palace fire of 1697 and survived. Today it belongs to the National Library of Sweden as A 148.
